linkedin.title: We are moving from searching for links to searching for answers.
linkedin.body:
For years, the internet taught us to be good at searching. We learned how to type keywords, scan a list of blue links, and click around until we found what we needed. It was an active process that required time and patience.

AI search is changing that dynamic entirely. Instead of giving you a list of sources to sift through, AI can now synthesize information from across the web and deliver a direct answer. It is a shift from browsing to understanding.

This is a massive upgrade for news consumption. The challenge with traditional search is that you often end up reading the same story five times from five different outlets just to piece together the full context of an event. AI allows us to cut through that repetition and get straight to the facts that matter.

But there is a catch. This technology relies on the quality of the information it is fed. If the underlying news is biased or incomplete, the AI answer will be too. That is why we are so focused on building systems that prioritize accuracy and diverse perspectives rather than just speed.

We believe the future of news is not just about finding information faster. It is about making sure the information you find is actually worth your time.
